Restructured to clearly separate: input requirements, output types with status codes, cost scenarios, and guidance on when to use list jobs. Clarified the credit batching mechanism for unsuccessful lookups.

data.current_description:
A person's name and company domain in, their work email out. 1 credit when the address is found and confirmed (`valid`). 1 credit when the domain accepts every address (`catch_all`); the most likely address comes back with `confirmed: false`. 0.25 credits when nothing is found. Free when the input is invalid, the domain has no email (`no_mail_domain`) or its mail server cannot be reached right now (`retry_later`). For more than a handful of people, start a list job.

The first lookup that finds nothing takes 1 credit and keeps 0.75 for the next three such lookups, so each costs 0.25.
data.summary_suggestion: Find a person's work email by name and domain
data.description_suggestion: Find a person's verified work email address using their name and company domain. Returns the email address with a confirmation status: `valid` (confirmed, 1 credit), `catch_all` (domain accepts all addresses, 1 credit, marked unconfirmed), or no result (0.25 credits). Free for invalid input, domains without email service, or unreachable mail servers. For bulk lookups of more than a few people, use the email-finder list job endpoint instead. Note: The first unsuccessful lookup costs 1 credit but reserves 0.75 credits for up to three subsequent unsuccessful lookups, making each additional miss cost only 0.25 credits.
data.reasoning: Original summary is too generic. Description is dense and hard for AI agents to parse due to complex cost structure and status codes. Restructured to clearly separate: input requirements, output types with status codes, cost scenarios, and guidance on when to use list jobs. Clarified the credit batching mechanism for unsuccessful lookups.

message: Operation 'create-email-finder-job' has semantic quality issues: missing_context, missing_input_details, poor_ai_interpretability. Summary is adequate but description lacks clarity about input format options and job control mechanisms. Added explicit guidance on the two input methods (rows vs CSV), clarified the difference between maximum_charge (estimate) and max_credits (hard limit), and explained pause conditions. Helps AI agents understand when to use this for bulk operations and how to control costs.

data.current_description: A background job for up to 10,000 people. Send `rows` (first_name and last_name, or name, plus domain and an optional ref of your own) or `csv` text with a header row. Same prices per row as a single lookup; `maximum_charge` is the most the list can cost. Set `max_credits` to cap the spend: the job pauses at that limit. It also pauses when credits run out, at the daily limit (it goes on after midnight UTC) or when most lookups find nothing. Repeated rows and rows without a usable name or domain are skipped for free.
data.summary_suggestion: Start a bulk email finder job for up to 10,000 people
data.description_suggestion: Create a background job to find work emails for multiple people (up to 10,000). Submit data as either structured rows (first_name and last_name or name, plus domain, plus optional ref) or CSV text with a header row. Pricing is identical to single lookups per row. Control spending with `maximum_charge` (estimated max cost) and `max_credits` (hard limit where job pauses). The job automatically pauses when credits run out, at the daily limit (resumes after midnight UTC), or when most lookups fail. Duplicate rows and rows with missing or invalid name/domain data are skipped at no cost. Returns a job ID for tracking progress.
data.reasoning: Summary is adequate but description lacks clarity about input format options and job control mechanisms. Added explicit guidance on the two input methods (rows vs CSV), clarified the difference between maximum_charge (estimate) and max_credits (hard limit), and explained pause conditions. Helps AI agents understand when to use this for bulk operations and how to control costs.

Note: The first unsuccessful lookup costs 1 credit but reserves 0.75 credits for up to three subsequent unsuccessful lookups, making each additional miss cost only 0.25 credits.
